entries.topic: The American bill in the US–Iran conflict, 1979–2026: deaths, costs, energy prices

claims.text: Operation Eagle Claw, 24–25 April 1980, tried to rescue 52 US embassy staff held in Tehran since 4 November 1979; at Desert One an RH-53D helicopter struck an EC-130, killing eight US servicemen (five Air Force, three Marines); the 52 were released 20 January 1981, minutes after Carter's term ended, after 444 days; Carter called the hostage-taking 'blackmail'

Kuwait asked the US in December 1986 to protect its tankers from Iranian attacks; the administration agreed 7 March 1987; Kuwaiti ships reflagged; Earnest Will ran 24 July 1987 (Navy began 23 July) to 26 September 1988; the reflagged MV Bridgeton struck an Iranian mine 24 July 1987, no injuries; Iranian PM Mousavi called the mine strike an 'irreparable blow to America's political and military prestige'
17 May 1987: an Iraqi jet fired two Exocet missiles at USS Stark, killing 37 sailors and injuring 21; Iraqi officials said the targeting was accidental
18 October 1987, Operation Nimble Archer: four destroyers shelled two Revolutionary Guard bases at the Rostam oil field

USS Samuel B. Roberts struck a mine 14 April 1988; ten sailors severely injured; Operation Praying Mantis 18 April 1988 destroyed two Iranian surveillance platforms (Sassan, Sirri), sank two Iranian ships and severely damaged a third

Proceedings (May 1989): Joshan sunk by Simpson and Wainwright after firing a Harpoon that missed; Sahand sank hours after air and Harpoon hits; Sabalan disabled by a laser-guided bomb and towed to Bandar Abbas

18 April 1988: Marine Capts. Stephen C. Leslie and Kenneth W. Hill killed when their AH-1T Sea Cobra (HML(A)-167) crashed at night about 15 miles southwest of Abu Musa; Navy officials reported no evidence of hostile fire; possibly lost evading Iranian fire

3 July 1988: USS Vincennes (Capt. William C. Rogers III) fired two missiles that shot down Iran Air 655; all 290 aboard died (274 passengers, 16 crew; 254 Iranians; 65 children); US said the crew misidentified the Airbus as an attacking F-14; Iran says it was intentional and unlawful, and at minimum negligent; Reagan expressed regret 5 July 1988; the US never formally apologised or acknowledged wrongdoing

1996: the US agreed to pay $131.8 million to discontinue Iran's 1989 ICJ case and other claims; $61.8 million compensated families of the 248 Iranians killed, ex gratia, without admitting liability; Rogers received the Legion of Merit, citation not mentioning the downing

Pentagon (Cmdr Sean Robertson, April 2019): 'DoD assessed that at least 603 U.S. personnel deaths in Iraq were the result of Iran-backed militants', up from ~500; State Dept: 17% of US personnel deaths in Iraq 2003–2011; attributed to EFPs, other IEDs, rockets, mortars, RPGs, small arms, snipers; the Pentagon did not provide the report to Military Times, which could not independently assess it

Task & Purpose: Brian Hook cited 'declassified U.S. military reports'; under Bush officials showed images of Iran-built EFPs but could not prove Iran supplied them to proxy forces; the reports carried no Iranian response

8 January 2020: Iran fired 15 missiles at two bases in Iraq, 10 at Al Asad, in retaliation for Soleimani's killing; Trump first said no Americans were harmed and posted 'All is well!'; by 10 February 2020 the Pentagon reported 109 troops diagnosed with mild traumatic brain injury

Iraqi PM's office said it received an 'official verbal message' from Iran that the response to Soleimani's assassination had begun or would begin shortly and would be limited to where the US military was located; Iraq, the US and others said they suffered no casualties

1 April 2024: suspected Israeli strike on Iran's consulate in Damascus killed Gen. Mohammad Reza Zahedi, his deputy and five other IRGC officers; Raisi: 'cowardly crime will not go unanswered'; Israel did not comment; per Axios via CBS the US told Iran it had no involvement or advance knowledge
AAA via wire report: US gasoline averaged about $2.98 before the war and $4.02 on 31 March 2026, first time above $4 since 2022; diesel $5.45, up from about $3.76
AAA: national average regular gasoline $4.564 on 21 May 2026, the 2026 high

EIA STEO 6 Oct 2026: retail gasoline averaged $4.35/gal in September 2026; annual 2025 $3.10, 2026 forecast $3.91; diesel averaged $6.29 in September, 2026 forecast $5.19; Brent 2025 $69/b, 2026 forecast $96/b, 4Q26 $105/b; assumes Middle East flows constrained through 4Q26 with convoys through Hormuz

entries.topic: Who pushed and who decided: Israeli and US advocacy, dissent, Congress and polling on war with Iran

claims.text: Trump, 3 March 2026, to reporters before meeting Merz: 'We were having negotiations with these lunatics, and it was my opinion that they were going to attack first'; 'So if anything, I might have forced Israel's hand'; Under Secretary Elbridge Colby: 'The president made our decision'; Sen. Angus King: 'I find it very disturbing that we're committing this nation to war based upon a decision by … a staunch ally'; Kaine: 'Have we learned nothing from 25 years of war in the Middle East?'

Rubio, 2 March 2026, Capitol Hill: 'We knew that there was going to be an Israeli action'; 'We knew that that would precipitate an attack against American forces'; 'There absolutely was an imminent threat'; Netanyahu in a video message said the coalition allowed him to do what he had 'yearned to do for 40 years'

FDD's Aaron Goren (5 March 2026) argued Israel did not drag the US into war: quotes Rubio's later clarification 'This had to happen no matter what'; cites months of US build-up, reported joint planning from December, and Israel's cancellation of strikes on 24 June 2025 when Trump asked

Joe Kent, NCTC director, resigned 17 March 2026: 'I cannot in good conscience support the ongoing war in Iran'; 'Iran posed no imminent threat to our nation'; the US started the war 'due to pressure from Israel and its powerful American lobby'

Responses to Kent: Trump said Kent was 'very weak on security' and 'Iran was a threat to every country'; J Street's Ilan Goldenberg said claims of an Israeli plot play 'on the worst antisemitic tropes' and that Trump is ultimately responsible; Sen. Warner agreed with Kent's opposition to the war; McConnell called the letter tainted by 'virulent anti-Semitism'

Gabbard resigned as DNI (reported 22 May 2026, effective 30 June) citing her husband's cancer diagnosis; neither she nor the reporting linked it to the Iran war; she had defended the war decision; Aaron Lukas acting director

June 2025: Marjorie Taylor Greene: 'I don't want to fight or fund nuclear-armed Israel's wars'; Bannon muted; Carlson silent after the strike; Massie a critic whom Trump called 'not Maga'; Vance called the strike 'a very precise, a very surgical strike tailored to an American interest'; Charlie Kirk praised it

Graham to Axios, 21 February 2026: voices counselling against entanglement 'seem to ignore the consequences of letting evil go unchecked'; unnamed advisers urged Trump to hold off and use the threat for concessions

Mark Levin, Fox News, 15 February 2026: 'Now is the time'; 'I cannot think of any reason not to take this regime out'; after June 2025 strikes Levin said 'there were a handful of us who encouraged this night' and that Trump did not need convincing (as quoted by Media Matters)
AIPAC press release 28 February 2026 backed the US strikes: 'Iran has American blood on its hands'; Iran 'will never acquire a nuclear weapon'
House vote on the Massie–Khanna Iran war powers resolution, 5 March 2026, failed 212–219; Democrats Cuellar, Landsman, Golden and Vargas voted no; Republicans Massie and Davidson yes

Senate passed Kaine's Iran war powers resolution 55–45 on 13 February 2020 with eight Republicans after the Soleimani strike; House passed it in March; Trump vetoed 6 May 2020 calling it 'insulting'; override failed 49–44 on 7 May; Kaine: 'It's not insulting. It's our job'; McConnell: 'misguided war powers resolution'

CNN/SSRS 22–23 June 2025 (1,030 adults): 56% disapprove, 44% approve of US strikes on Iran; 58% expect Iran to become more of a threat; 65% say Congress should have to approve further action (21% not)
